web_evidence.title: 1Q84 | Penguin Random House Secondary Education
web_evidence.note: The authorized Chapter 1 excerpt sustains external third-person narration of Aomame, including her actions, history, perceptions, and thoughts.

web_evidence.title: Metaficción e intertextualidad en la novela 1Q84 de Haruki Murakami
web_evidence.note: A University of Costa Rica journal article explicitly states that the entire novel has an omniscient narrator and a three-focus structure through Aomame, Tengo, and Ushikawa; the focal shifts do not change grammatical person.

web_evidence.title: Satellites of Love
web_evidence.note: This opened literary review explicitly contrasts Murakami's usual first-person quests with the third-person 1Q84, describes Aomame and Tengo's alternating chapters, and notes Ushikawa's added perspective.

web_evidence.title: 1Q84 by Haruki Murakami – review
web_evidence.note: The review identifies Ushikawa as a third focus of third-person narration in Book 3 and supplies sustained third-person prose examples involving Tengo and Aomame.

search_log: Searched for "1Q84 Haruki Murakami official excerpt Aomame Tengo third person" and publisher/first-chapter variants; opened Penguin Random House's authorized Chapter 1 excerpt.
Searched for "1Q84 point of view third person alternating chapters narrator scholarly" and structural variants covering Aomame, Tengo, and Ushikawa.
Opened the University of Costa Rica journal PDF and verified its whole-book statement that the novel uses an omniscient narrator with three focal perspectives.
Opened Bookforum and Guardian reviews to verify third-person narration beyond the opening and the addition of Ushikawa's Book 3 perspective.
The University of Oregon J-lit page and Los Angeles Review of Books page returned fetch errors during opening, so their search snippets were not used as evidence.

Exact-phrase searches for "I can bear any pain as long as it has meaning" and "The thing I'm most afraid of is me" recovered surrounding dialogue, showing that q00392 and q00427 are character speech misbucketed as events.

An exact-phrase search for q00419 located the passage in Murakami's separate short story "On Seeing the 100% Perfect Girl One Beautiful April Morning," indicating likely Goodreads provenance contamination.
person_note: The controlling narration is third person throughout, while chapters alternate focal attention among Aomame and Tengo and, in Book 3, Ushikawa. The strongest event passages independently show external narration of characters' actions and private states. The first-person event-bucket snippets are clipped speech or direct character thought rather than autonomous first-person sections; web context explicitly resolves q00392 and q00427 as dialogue. q00419 appears to come from a separate Murakami short story and is therefore not evidence about this novel. Authorized opening prose, whole-book scholarly analysis, and reputable structural reviews agree, with no credible evidence of sustained first- or second-person base narration.
